 Meeting Schedule

The regular meetings of the City Council are held on the second and fourth Tuesday of each month,
closed session business will usually commence at 5:30 p.m., when scheduled, and general business
session will commence at 6:30 p.m.

Brown Act

Agendas are drafted to accurately state what the legislative body is being asked to consider. The
legislative body can take action on "all items" listed on the agenda and be in compliance with the open
meeting laws. Under the Brown Act, no action may be taken on a matter unless it is listed on the
agenda, or unless certain emergency or special circumstances exist. The governing body may direct
staff to investigate and/or schedule certain matters for consideration at a future meeting.

City's Vision Statement

Coming Soon

Public Communications

Public Comments on agenda items are limited to three (3) minutes. All comments are to be addressed
directly to the Agency Members not to the members of the public.

Meeting Compensation Disclosure

Pursuant to Government Code Section 54952.3: Disclosure of compensation for meeting
attendance by City Council Members is $650 monthly regardless of the amount of meetings.

Proclamations, Certificates, Introductions And Ceremonial Actions
NONE

Public Hearings
NONE

Comments From The Audience - Non-Agenda Items
During this time, members of the public may address the City Council regarding any items not
listed on the agenda and within the subject matter jurisdiction of the City Council and not on
this agenda. Comments from the audience will be limited to three (3) minutes per speaker;
unless authorized by the Mayor, the time limit may not be extended by utilizing another
member's time. There will be no debate or action on items not listed on the agenda unless
authorized by law. The collective initial period of time for comments from the audience shall
be limited to 45 minutes. Any speaker that did not get a chance to speak during this segment
due to the 45-minute limitations will be able to speak at the end of the meeting prior to
adjournment.

Note: The City Council desires to provide all members of the public with the opportunity to
address the Council. Nevertheless, obscene language, comments intended to
disrupt/interfere, other actions which disrupt the progress of the meeting or slanderous

  2
 comments will not be tolerated and may result in ejection and/or may constitute a violation of
South Gate Municipal Code Section1.04.110.

Reports And Comments From City Officials
During this time, members of the City Council will report on matters pertaining to their service
on various intergovernmental boards and commissions as a representative of the City
pursuant to Assembly Bill 1234. City Council Members will also have an opportunity to
comment on matters not on the agenda.

Consent Calendar Items
Agenda Items 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7 and 8 are Consent Calendar Items. All items including
Ordinances, Resolutions and Contracts, may be approved by adoption of the Consent
Calendar, individually and collectively by one (1) motion. There will be no separate discussion
of these items unless Members of the City Council, the public, or staff request that specific
items be removed from the Consent Calendar for separate discussion and action. Members
of the public are permitted to speak on any item listed but their time period is limited to three
(3) minutes in total.

Any motion to introduce or adopt an Ordinance on the Consent Calendar shall be: (1) a
motion to waive the reading of the Ordinance and introduce the Ordinance or (2) a motion to
waive the reading of the Ordinance and adopt the Ordinance, as appropriate.

 GENERAL NOTICE TO THE PUBLIC

The City Council adopted new rules relating to the conduct of the public meetings, proceedings, and
business in the City of South Gate on July 12, 2022, (Resolution 2022-38-CC) and go into effect on
August 1, 2022. Resolution #2022-38-CC is available at the City Clerk’s Office.

MEETING SCHEDULE

Regular meetings of the City Council are held on the second and fourth Tuesday of each month, closed
session meetings will commence at 5:30 p.m. unless posted otherwise on its agenda. The regular City
Council meetings will commence at 6:30 p.m. Agendas are available at the following locations: City Clerk
Office, Public Notice Boards at City Hall, and on the City’s web page at https://www.cityofsouthgate.org

The Public can sign up to receive automatic notices of postings of agendas for the City Council or any
other Commission or Board of the City of South Gate. Visit the City webpage and click on the Agenda &
Minutes icon. That will take you the page where an individual can enter their email in the “Email
Updates” box to register.

PUBLIC COMMENT/PARTICIPATION

Any person may request to address a legislative body during a public meeting. The Presiding Officer will
call upon those present in the Council Chambers first. After all speakers in the Chambers have spoken,
the Presiding Officer will call upon those participating via zoom or teleconference.

Speakers are limited to three (3) minutes on any item listed on the agenda, including public hearings.
Under Comments from the Audience portion, speakers are also limited to a single three (3) minutes time
limit. Comments from the Audience is initially limited to 45 minutes at each meeting. Any speaker still
wishing to speak, that did not speak, will have an addition Comments from the Audience opportunity after
the last business item is finished. The Presiding Officer may extend the time limit as long as there is no
objection from the City Council as a body.

To ensure that the public is able to participate, the City provides the opportunity to submit their
comments in person, virtually, email, phone call, mail and any other method which may become
available. Methods of participation may be subject to change during other such times when a State of
Emergency, Health Order or State Executive Order limits in-person participation.

CURFEW

In absence of a motion duly adopted by majority vote of the City Council, the Presiding Officer may
adjourn the City Council meetings at 10:30 p.m. The Presiding Officer may ask the City Council if any
agenda items listed should be continued or dealt with during the meeting. For those items to be
continued, the City Council can direct the item be placed on the next City Council agenda or the current
meeting may be adjourned to a time certain at which time the meeting shall be reconvened as an
Adjourned Regular Meeting of the City Council and action upon the published agenda continued.

STAFF REPORTS

As a general rule, staff reports. or other written documentation are prepared/organized with respect to
each item of business listed on the agenda. Meeting agendas and staff reports are available at least 72-
hours prior to the scheduled regular City Council meeting and a minimum of 24-hours prior to a Special
City Council meeting. There are times when the City Council receives written material. revised material
after the posting of agendas, these materials are become a public record and will be available for public
view within 72-hours after the meeting in which they were received. Those materials and any other public

  8
 document can be inspected in the City Clerk's Office located at 8650 California Avenue, South Gate.

SERVICES TO FACILITATE ACCESS TO PUBLIC MEETINGS

In compliance with the American with Disabilities Act, if you need special assistance to participate in the
City Council Meetings, please contact the Office of the City Clerk. Notification 48 hours prior to the City
Council Meeting will enable the City to make reasonable arrangements to assure accessibility. For
further information, please contact the Office of the City Clerk at (323) 563-9510 or via email at
yglaze@sogate.org.

 BACKGROUND:  The  proposed  zoning  code  amendment  was  presented  and  unanimously
approved  at the July 26, 2022,  City  Council  meeting.  The ordinance  provides  additional  solutions
to parking  requirements  for non-residential  uses throughout  the City.

On July 5, 2022,  the Planning  Commission  adopted  Planning  Commission  Resolution  No. 2022-
13, recommending  the City  Council  approve  Zoning  Code  Amendment  No.  175  and adopt  an
Ordinance,  amending  Section  11.33  (Parking  Standards)  of Title  11 (Zoning)  to add minimum
parking  requirements  for specific  land use types,  which  are not currently  listed  within  the SGMC
Section  11.33.040  "Required  parking  by  land  use,"  to  amend  off-site  parking  distance
requirements  and standards  within  SGMC  Section  11.33.060  "Parking  lot standards;"  and also to
simplify  by  amending  parking  requirement  calculations  per  SGMC  Section  11.33.040  (D)(I)
"Calculations."

Under  Section  11.33.040,  Table  11.33-1  "Minimum  Required  Parking  by Land Use"  lists various
land uses, ranging  from  banks  and offices  to stadiums  and warehouses.  However,  land uses that
are specific  to children,  older  adults,  community  assembly  or people  with  disabilities  are not
adequately  or similarly  listed  in Table  11.33-1.  Parking  calculations  are detertnined  by staff who
are often unable  to simplify  determinations  of parking  requirements

SGMC  Section  11.33.060  provides  "Off-site  Parking  Distance"  standards  for land uses serving
children,  older  adults,  community  assembly  or people  with  disabilities  and non-residential  uses.
Although  these land uses are noted  in this code section,  the distance  allowed  between  sites does
not adequately  reflect  real-life  distances  that may be permitted  pursuant  to the Zoning  Code.

ANALYSIS:
Required  Parking  based on Land Uses
Land  uses  that  are specific  to  children,  older  adults,  community  assembly  or  people  with
disabilities  include,  but are not limited  to, uses such as children  or adult day care centers;  nursery
schools;  preschools;  infant  centers;  religious  facilities;  lodges;  meeting  halls;  community,  cultural,
performing  arts centers;  etc. Table 11.33-1,  under SGMC  Sectionll.33.040,  "Schools"  and "Trade
and/or  vocational  schools"  are listed  as below:

  Land  Use  Type  Minimum  Required  Parking
  Schools  l per employee

  Trade and/or vocational  schools  3, plus 1 per student capacity; or l per l sq. ft.
  building gfa, whichever is greater

Day care centers  and community  centers  are relatively  similar  land uses to the uses listed  above,
however,  there  are staffing  differences  that  would  cause  for  substantial  parking  requirement
differences.  For example,  the minimum  required  parking  for schools  is based on the number  of
employees,  which  can be calculated  based on the number  of classrooms  at a school  facility.  Day
care centers,  meeting  halls and perfornning  arts centers  are not solely  based around  classrooms  and
employees  assigned  accordingly.  These  land  uses that  are specific  to children,  the elderly,  or
people  with  disabilities  may require  multiple  employees/instructors/teachers/etc.,

Off-site  Parking  Distances
Because  parking  is often at a shortage  throughout  the City,  various  uses are unable  to meet parking
requirements  pursuant  to the Zoning  Code. The Zoning  Code currently  allows  for a shared parking
option,  which  is listed  in Table  11.33-3,  under  SGMC  11.33.060.  This  shared  parking  option
allows  uses to enter into  agreements  with  nearby  uses that have a surplus  of parking  spaces. For
example,  a restaurant  that  is unable  to provide  parking  based  on the Zoning  Code  parking
requirements  may request  to share parking  with  a nearby  retail market  that has more parking  spaces
than it is required  to provide.  The "Off-site  Parking  Distance"  for nonresidential  uses is 300 feet
from  the site. Therefore,  the restaurant  would  have to be located  a maximum  of 300 feet from  the
retail  market.  Utilizing  nearby  excess  parking  spaces  allows  the  restaurant  to meet  parking
requirements  per the Zoning  Code.

Minagar  & Associates,  Inc. completed  a survey  of off-site  parking  distances  from  various  cities
tbroughout  the State and detertnined  that the City's  current  standard  for off-site  parking  distance
allowances  is lower  than most  cities.  The study recommends  a maximum  of 700 feet in distance
between  uses, however  Staff  has determined  that less than a quarter  of a mile,  linearl,000  feet,
would  allow  manyuses  in the City to achieve  parking  compliance  with  the Zoning  Code. To ensure
that shared parking  between  uses is maintained,  a parking  covenant  agreement  would  be submitted
to the City  for administrative  review  and ultimately  approved  by the Community  Development
Director.

In addition  to the above  off-site  parking  distance  allowance,  uses would  also be able to share
parking  with  other  uses within  1,000  feet that are able to provide  parking  availability  based on
differences  in hours  of operation.  For example,  a religious  facility  that operates  between  5 a.m.
and 5 p.m. would  be able to share parking  spaces with  a restaurant  that operates  between  6 p.m.
and 11 p.m. The parking  spaces would  be shared by each use at different  times  of each day of the
week.  The 1,000  linear  foot off-site  parking  distance  referenced  above,  where  there is a surplus  of
parking  spaces, in the case of differences  in hours of operation  and days of the week,  a Conditional
Use Permit  approval  would  be required.  A parking  covenant  agreement  between  the two  uses
would  also be required.

Minimum  Parking  Requirement  Calculations
The SGMC  Section  11.33.040  also instructs  staff to calculate  minimum  required  parking  based on
gross floor  area calculations,  seating  calculations  and assembly  area calculations.  Based  on the
current  Zoning  Code,  for example,  when  calculating  the minimum  number  of required  parking
spaces for a library,  one parking  space is required  per 250 square  feet of gross floor  area (GFA).
This  GFA  includes  all square  footage  within  surrounding  exterior  walls  of the library  building,
including  shared  bathroom  spaces,  storage  areas and areas for  circulation.  Therefore  a 10,000
square  foot  library  would  be required  to provide  40 parking  spaces  on-site.  As noted  above,
meeting  parking  requirements  per the current  Zoning  Code is often difficult  to achieve  throughout
the City.

Therefore,  staff is recommending  that parking  calculations  be amended  to simplify  calculations  of
GFA  in SGMC  Section  11.33.040  (D)(1)  as follows:

D.  Calculations.

  1.  Gross Floor  Area Calculations.  Gross  floor  area calculations  are based on the area within
  the surrounding  exterior  walls  of a building  or any portion  thereof,  ineluding  sharcd
  bathroom  spaces, storage  arcas, and areas for circulation.  Required  parking  is calculated
  based on publicly  accessible  areas and areas that are not accessible  to the public.

For example,  a 1,000  square foot retail  store that includes  a 250 square foot  employee  office,  250
square  feet for restrooms  for both the public  and employees  and the remaining  500 square  feet is
the retail  shop area. The restrooms  and retail  shop area, which  are both areas that are accessible  to
the public,  would  be calculated  based on the minimum  parking  required  for retail  stores (1 per 200
square feet GFA).  The remaining  250 square foot employee  office,  not publicly  accessible,  would

 be calculated  based  on the minimum  parking  required  for  offices  (1 per  300  square  feet  GFA).
This  calculation  would  lower  the number  of minimum  parking  spaces  required.

The  proposed  amendments  will  address  parking  sufficiency  for  non-residential  uses throughout
the City  and also provide  for additional  options  for parking  compliance  with  the Zoning  Code.

SUBJECT:  RESOLUTION  DESIGNATING  VOTING  DELEGATES  FOR  THE  ANNUAL
BUSINESS  MEETNG/GENERAL  ASSEMBLY  AT  THE  2022  LEAGUE  OF  CALIFORNIA
CITIES  ANNUAL  CONFERENCE  AND EXPO

PURPOSE:  To designate eligible elected officials as voting delegates  for  the upcoming  2022
League of California Cities Annual Conference on September 7-9, 2022.

RECOMMENDED  ACTION:  The City  Council  will  consider  adopting  a Resolution  designating  a
member  of the City Council  as the voting  delegate for the Annual  Business  Meeting/General  Assembly
during the 2022 League of California  Cities Annual Conference and Expo and up to two (2) alternate
voting delegates should the primary designee be unable to represent the City.

FISCAL  IMPACT:  None

ANALYSIS:  An important  part of the League of California  Cities Annual  Conference  is the Annual
Business  Meeting/General  Assembly  where  membership  considers  and  acts on resolutions  that
establish  Cal Cities'  policy.  These resolutions  guide cities and the League  in their efforts  to improve
the quality,  responsiveness,  and vitality  of local governrnent  in California.  Each member  city has the
right to cast one vote on matters pertaining  to the League  of California  Cities  policies  that are being
considered by the General Assembly.

Historically,  the City  has designated  the two  City  Council  members  who  serve as delegate  and
alternate to the LA County  Division  of the League of California  Cities.  Those two members  are Vice
Mayor Maria del Pilar Avalos who would represent the City as the voting  delegate  and Council
Member Denise Diaz who would serve as the first altemate delegate.

BACKGROUND:  Every year, the League  of California  Cities requires  that the City designate  voting
delegates  to vote and take action  during  the Annual  Conference  and Expo.  The proposed  Resolution
designates  Vice Mayor  Avalos  as the voting  delegate and Council  Member  Diaz as the alternate  voting
delegate.  The City Council can designate another member who is attending  the conference  as a second
alternate,  in case Council Member Diaz is unexpectedly  unavailable.

SUBJECT:  AGREEMENT  WITH  JOHN  L. HUNTER  AND  ASSOCIATES,  INC.,  FOR
STORM  WATER  MANAGEMENT  SERVICES  FOR  THE  MUNICIPAL  SEPARATE
STORM  SEWER  SYSTEM  (MS4)  PERMIT  PROGRAM

PURPOSE:  To approve  an Agreement  with  John L. Hunter  and Associates,  Inc.  ("JLHA"),  to
provide  storm  water  management  services  for the management  of the City's  National  Pollution
Discharge  Elimination  System  ("NPDES")  Program.  The current  agreement  expires  on August  23,
2022.

RECOMMEDED  ACTIONS:  The City  Council  will  consider:
  a.  Approving  an agreement  with  John L. Hunter  and Associates,  Inc. ("Agreement"),  for storm
  water  management  services  required  by the National  Pollution  Discharge  Elimination
  System  (NPDES)  Permit,  for a three-year  term,  in an amount  not-to-exceed  $334,155,  or
  $111,385 annually;  and
  b.  Authorizing  the Mayor  to execute  the Agreement  in a form  acceptable  to the City Attorney.

FISCAL  IMPACT:  There  is no impact  to the General  Fund.  The proposed  Agreement  is in the
amount  of $334,155,  or $111,385  annually,  which  will  be funded  with  Measure  W Funds.  The
$111,385 cost of the Agreement  will  be included  in the Fiscal  Year 2022/23 Municipal  Budget  and
will  be funded  from  the Measure  W Fund in Account  No. 21 7-727-57-6101.

ANALYSIS:  The City  owns  and operates  a storm  drain  system  that is regulated  by the NPDES
Permit  which  is issued by the State Water  Resources  Control  Board.  TheNPDES  Permitrequiresthe
City  to have  various  programs  in  place  such  as a Watershed  Management  Plan  ("WMP"),
Industrial/Commercial  Facilities  Program,  Planning  and  Land  Development  Program,  Load
Reduction  Strategy  Implementation  Program  and Integrated  Monitoring  Program.  It also requires
compliance  through  City operations  and projects.  The complexity  of the NPDES  Program  warrants
an environmental  firm  with  special  technical  expertise  and experience  in the NPDES  program.  A
Request  for Proposal  was issued for storm  water management  services.  JLHA  is recommended  for
thecontract.  JLHAhasmanagedtheCity'sNPDESProgramandMS4Permitsinceitsinceptionin
1991  and  has  been  instrumental  to  keeping  the  City  in  compliance  with  state  and  federal
requirements.

  1
  51
 BACKGROUND:  Storm  water  management  is a complex  administrative,  technical  and legal
matter,  with  local, state and federal  requirements.  In 2021, the Los Angeles  Regional  Water  Quality
Controls  Board  ("Regional  Board")  re-issued  an MS4  Permit  to the City.  The permit  regulates
pollutant  discharges  from  storm  water runoff  into the Los Angeles  River  and Rio Hondo  Channel.
Services  of a specialty  consultant  are warranted  to managethe  program  and achieve compliance,  due
to the  complexity  of  the  MS4  Permit.  JLHA  ensures  the  City  will  meet  state  and  federal
requirements

The cost of JLHA's  services  is $111,385  annually  and includes  the Industrial/Commercial  Facilities
Program  ($51,175),  Planning  and Land Development  Program  ($38,015),  Load Reduction  Strategy
Implementation  Assistance  Program  ($8,580), Implement  Integrated  Monitoring  Program  ($1,250),
Statewide  Trash  Amendment  submittal  ($7,070),  Administration  (includes  annual  reporting)
($14,915)  and Illicit  Connection  and Illicit  Discharge  Elimination  Program  ($3,300).  JLHA  also
added a services  discount  of $12,920  because JLHA  conducts  combined  inspections  at facilities  that
require  both NPDES  (stormwater)  and Industrial  Waste  Discharge  ("IWD")  inspections.  It saves
time and money  to do both at the same time;  therefore,  the City receives  a savings  in the form  of a
discount.

In addition,  JLHA  offers  the following:

  *  JLHA  has managed  the City's  NPDES  programs  for over three decades  and was the lead
  consultant  in the development  of the City's  WMP.

  *  JLHAhasexperienceinmanagingNPDESprogramsforover30agencieswithservicesthat
  include  field  services  inspection  for Best Management  Practice  ("BMP"),  developmentplan
  review,  public  outreach,  creating  program  reports,  watershed  plan  development/
  implementation,  producing  field  studies,  providing  stafftraining,  and assisting  cities through
  Regional  Water  Board  audits.

  *  There are several  layers  for compliance  including  regional  solutions  that require  the City to
  collaborate  with  agencies  within  the Lower  Los Angeles  River  Subwatershed  subcommittee,
  led  by  JLHA.  The  City  is a member  of the  Gateway  Water  Management  Authority
  ("GWMA")  who  leads local,  sub-regional  and regional  collaboration  efforts.  JLHA  was
  selected  to represent  four  out of the five watershed  subcommittees.

  *  The owner  of JLHA,  Mr.  John Hunter,  is currently  the Chair  of the Los Angeles  Permit
  Group  which  provides  area wide MS4 Permit  updates to all agencies  under the Los Angeles
  Region  MS4  Permit.  JLHA  also manages  MS4  Permit  Programs  for 30 other cities  in the
  region.

management,  sewer  overflow  prevention,  water  conservation,  and  recycling.  Services  include
program  administration,  planning,  reporting,  and funding,  as well  as inspections,  engineering,
monitoring,  and public  education.

 ANALYSIS:  The proposed  Agreement  is in the amount  of $34,500 as that is the total  cost of
providing  the  services  documented  in the  scope  of  work  in the  Agreement.  However,  the
Agreement  documents  that the City  will  fund  $19,500  for services  and that Hub  Cities  will  fund
$15,000 through an in-kind construction. This structure for the Agreement is needed to ensure
that the total amount to be funded by the City is $19,500 even though the total cost for the
services  is $34,500.

BACKGROUND:  As part of the City's  effort  to address  blight  and improve  litter  removal,  staff
is proposing  a program  to begin  enforcement  of the  City's  municipal  code  as it relates  to
abandoned,  unpermitted,  and/or  unmaintained  newsracks  and  pay  phones  placed  within  the
public  right-of-way.

As a result  of technology  advancing  access to news  and other  periodicals  along  with  increased
accessibility  to mobile  phone  devices,  newsracks  and pay phones  have become  almost  obsolete.
These  devices  once used by private  companies  to provide  news  and phone  service  have,  been
abandoned  in  place  and  are now  covered  with  graffiti,  stickers,  and  flyers/notices  and  are
damaged  and in general  disrepair.  In  some  cases,  unpermitted  companies  use newsracks  for
publications  and the material  is often  discarded  into  the public  right-of-way;  a problem  City
crews  and City  contractors  must address.

Chapter  5.07 (Newsracks)  was added to the City's  municipal  code in 2000 and Chapter  5.34 (Pay
Phones  in the Public  Right-of-Way)  was added in 2006.  Consequently,  the codes have not been
regularly  enforced  for  the  past  5 years.  Each  of  these  codes  provides  a process  where  the
permittee  is required  to apply  and pay for annual  permits  and maintain  the devices.  The City  has
lost revenue  from  unpermitted  devices  and the ability  to require  the permittee  to maintain  the
devices  as required  in the municipal  code.

Per  the  SGMC,  newsracks  may  not  interfere  with  pedestrian  or  vehicular  traffic,  transit
operations,  or handicapped  access.  Newsracks  are to be maintained  and  free  of  graffiti  or
stickers,  rust,  trash  or dirt.  They  must  have  a door  or other  covering  to keep  the publications
inside  the newsrack  and the elements  out.  Plastic  windows  must be transparent  and unbroken.  A
newsrack  may not be chained  to any other object.  When  a permittee  removes  a newsrack,  it must
be done without  damage  to the sidewalk.  If there is damage,  the permittee  must  restore  the site
to the same condition  as the surrounding  area.

Similar  conditions  of maintenance  and non-interference  with  the flow  of pedestrian  or vehicle
access apply  to phone  booths.

The Public  Works  Department  has a list of permitted  newsracks  which  was last updated  in 2016.
The total  number  of permitted  newsracks  citywide  totals  376. The Department  does not have a
database  on  pay  phone  booths  within  the  public  right-of-way.  A  preliminary  estimate  of
unpermitted  pay phones  in the right-of-way  is approximately  175 locations.  As stated earlier,  the
last record  of payment  for a newsrack  permit  is in 2016.

To implement  an efficient  and effective  removal  program,  a survey  of the City's  right-of-ways  to
identify  the locations,  condition  and permittee  identification  information  must  be conducted  to

  2

  102
 begin  the noticing  process  under  the municipal  code.  Staffing  vacancies  and workload  prevent
the City  from  using  existing  staff  without  delaying  other projects  or tasks.  Using  Hub  Cities  to
undertake  the survey  will  allow  the City  to accomplish  several  goals.

The first  goal is to begin  to bring  these devices  into  compliance  with  our municipal  code.  This
includes  properly  obtaining  permits  and maintaining  compliant  devices.  Second,  this Agreement
allows  the City  to further  promote  workforce  development  of the young  adult population  through
Hub  Cities.  Participants  will  learn  basic  research  skills  in  developing  a new  database  and
comparing  it against the existing  permit  inventory  for accuracy.  Finally,  the most important  goal
is the elimination  of blight  in the City.  It is likely  that a significant  portion  of the newsracks  and
pay  phones  are  completely  abandoned.  Once  the  City  follows  the  noticing  process  and
noncompliance  period  has  passed,  removal  of  these  devices  will  make  a  measurable
improvement  in the effort  to reduce  paper waste and graffiti  in the public  right-of-way.

The majority  of devices  are located  on commercial  streets  including  Atlantic  Avenue,  Firestone
Boulevard,  Tweedy  Boulevard,  Long  Beach  Boulevard,  Alarneda  Street,  Imperial  Highway,  and
Garfield  Avenue.

The preliminary  schedule  for program  implementation  is tentatively  proposed  as follows:
  *  Field  Survey  completed  by Hub Cities  within  60-days  after agreement  approval
  @  Notice  to last known  or current  permittee  to be done over 90-days
  *  Removal  of unpermitted  devices  to be done over 90-days
  *  Repairs  to public  right-of-  way over the 90-days  (concurrent  with  removal)
  @  Disposal  of unclaimed  devices  60-days  after removal.

The proposed  schedule  would  take  between  August  2022  and January  2023  to complete,  with
City  Council  approval.

As used in this chapter:

"Newsrack"  means  any type of unmanned  device  placed  upon any public  right-of-way  for the vending  of or free
distribution  of newspapers  or news periodicals.

"Public  right-of-way"  means  any public  street,  highway,  sidewalk,  parkway,  or alley.

5.07.020 Permit  required.

A.  It is unlawful for any person to place, affix, erect, construct,  or maintain a newsrack  upon any public right-
of-way within the city unless there has been issued, and is in valid existence,  a newsrack  permit from the
department  of public works, in addition to any other city permitting  requirements,  including,  but not limited to, a
business  license or business  permit.

B.  The newsrack  permit shall be valid for the period indicated  on the permit and only for the particular  locations
specified  thereon.

(Ord. 2065 § 1 (part), 9'12-00)

5.07.030 Application  for permit.

No newsrack  permit shall be issued except upon a written application  filed with, and upon a form prescribed  by
the department  of public works. The department  of public works shall take action upon the application  within
thirty days of submission  of the completed  application.  Such application  shall contain the following:

A.  The name, address  and telephone  number of the applicant;

B.  A site map or drawing showing the exact location of each newsrack  to be installed or maintained  in the city
by the applicant.  The applicant  shall also provide the following  information:  the width of the sidewalk;  the
existence  of other newsracks  at the proposed  location, and any and all structures,  encroachments  or objects of
any kind or character  located within twenty-five  feet of the proposed  installation,  including,  but not limited to,
traffic signals,  street light poles,  u.s. postal boxes,  police call-boxes,  fire call-boxes,  fire hydrants,  bus stops,
bus benches,  utility poles, telephones,  parking meters, emergency  facilities,  building entrances,  and driveways.
The site map or drawing should also indicate the location of marked crosswalks  and curb returns of unmarked
crosswalks.  If feasible,  the applicant  may submit photographs  depicting  such items;

C.  A description  of each proposed  newsrack,  including  its dimensions  and type;

D.  The signature  of the owner of the newsrack  for which permits  are sought; and

E.  A written statement  agreeing to hold harmless  and indemnify  the city for any newsrack(s)  to be installed  or
maintained  over any public right-of-way  in accordance  with Section  .

(Ord. 2065 § 1 (part), 9-12-00)

Each application  for a newsrack  permit shall be accompanied  by a nonrefundable  fee, the amount of which shall

A.  The application  for a newsrack  permit shall be denied if the department  of public works finds that the

B.  The application  for newsrack  permit shall be denied if it is determined  that the city intends to use said
portion of the public right-of-way  for a public purpose.

C.  The application  for newsrack  permit may be denied for failure to comply with any of the requirements  of this
section.

(Ord. 2065 § 1 (part), 9-12-00)

5.07.060 General  placement.

Subject to the prohibitions  set forth in Section  of this chapter,  newsracks  shall only be placed near a
curb or adjacent to the wall of a building.  Newsracks  placed near the curb must be placed parallel to and no
closer than eighteen inches from the edge of the curb and no farther than twenty-four  inches from the edge of the
curb, measured from the curb edge to the nearest point on the newsrack.  Newsracks  placed adjacent to the wall
of a building shall be placed parallel to and no closer than six inches from the wall and no farther than eighteen
inches from the wall. The maximum  number of newsracks  in any location  is six newsracks.  With respect to any
newsrack  existing prior to the effective  date of the ordinance  codified  in this chapter, the director  of public works
shall have the discretion  to waive any requirement  of this section or Section  provided that the
placement  of the existing  newsrack  does not tend to unreasonably  obstruct  or interfere with the flow of
pedestrian  or vehicular  traffic  along any public way, create a hazard, or is otherwise  detrimental  to the public
safety, welfare or convenience.

(Ord. 2065 § 1 (part), 9-12-00)

5.34.010 Purpose.

The intent and purpose of this chapter is to establish  a permit procedure  for obtaining advance permission  from
the city prior to the placement  of any pay phone or similar device (all of which are for ease of reference  referred
to as "pay phones" in this chapter)  in the public right-of-way,  to declare any pay phone installed in the public
right-of-way  without prior city approval to be a public nuisance as defined by Sections  3479 and 3480 of the
California  Civil Code; and to set forth a method for the removal of any nonpermitted  pay phones that have been
or may be placed on the public right-of-way.  The procedure  set forth in this chapter for removal applies to any
pay phone placed in the public right-of-way  that the city council declares  to be a public nuisance either by the
provision  of this chapter or any other ordinance  that the city may thereafter  adopt. The procedure  set forth in this
chapter is not intended to be exclusive  and is in addition to the procedure  for public nuisance abatement  that is
conferred  upon the city by Section 3494 of the California  Civil Code, Section 731 of the California  Code of Civil
Procedure,  Section 38773 of the California  Government  Code, or any other lawful authority conferred  to the city
by state statutes  or this chapter.

(Ord. 2214 § 2 (part), 7-25-06)

5.34.020 Unlawful  maintenance  of pay phones  in the public  right-of-way-Misdemeanor-Permit  required.
It shall be unlawful and a misdemeanor  for any person owning, leasing, occupying,  or exercising  control over any
property  adjoining any portion of the public right-of-way  to permit, lease, authorize,  install, locate, maintain or
operate any pay phone on a public right-of-way  without having first obtained a permit in writing to do so from the
public works director or his designee.

(Ord. 2214 § 2 (part), 7-25-06)

director or his designee.  The application  shall include the following  information:

B.  An elevation  of the proposed pay phone design, including lighting, colors,  and design;

number of the proposed vending company  responsible  for installation,  maintenance,  and billing of the proposed
pay phone(s) ;

D.  A written statement  whereby the applicant  agrees to indemnify,  protect,  defend, and hold harmless  the city
of South Gate, its officers,  officials,  employees,  and agents, from any loss or liability or damage, including

5.34.080  Appeals.

The applicant  or any person  dissatisfied  with the determination  of the public  works  director  (or his designee)

relative  to the application  for a pay phone permit,  the revocation  of a previously  issued  pay phone permit,  or the

determination  to remove  a pay phone as a public  nuisance,  may appeal to the city council  from said

hearing,  shall be paid at the time of filing an appeal.  A notice  of the date, time,  and location  of the scheduled

appeal shall be sent at least fourteen  days prior to the scheduled  hearing  date to the appealing  party,  and nearby

residents  or businesses  by mailing  a letter  notice,  first class  mail to the appealing  party,  the original  applicant,

roll of Los Angeles  County.  The city council's  determination  following  a hearing  shall be final and conclusive  in

SUBJECT:  AGREEMENTS  FOR  BUILDING  PLAN  CHECK  SERVICES

PURPOSE:  To  award  two  separate  Professional  Services  Agreements  ("Agreements")  for  on-call
plan review  and inspection  services  to support  the Comtnunity  Development  Department.

RECOMMENDED  ACTIONS:  The City  Council  will  consider:
  a.  Approving  an Agreement  with  Melad  & Associates,  hic., to provide  building  plan check and
  inspection  services  in the amount  not to exceed $750,000  for a three-year  term;
  b.  Approving  Agreement  with  True North  Compliance  Services  to provide  building  plan check
  and inspection  services  in the amount  not to exceed  $750,000  for a three-year  term;  and
  c.  Authorizing  the Mayor  to execute  the Agreements  in a form  acceptable  to the City Attorney.

FISCAI,  IMPACT:  The total  contract  amount  over the three-year  term  will  not exceed  $1,500,000.
The costs for plan check  services  for the first  year of this agreement  are included  in the FY 2022-2023
budget  and will  be offset  by revenues  from  plan check fees.

ANALYSIS:  The proposed  Agreement  supports  the City  Council  goals  of "encouraging  economic
development"  and  of  "development  and  protecting  strong  sustainable  neighborhoods."  This  is
accomplished  by providing  high quality  plan check  services  that ensure new construction  is designed  to
meet safety  standards  with  the City's  Building  Code.  In addition,  building  plan  check  services  will  be
provided  in a reduced  period  of time to benefit  residents,  investors,  developers,  and contractors.  Another
City  Council  goal is to enhance,  accelerate  and update  services  to the latest technology  available  (such
as electronic  plan  check  to expedite  the plan  check  process  for  investors,  developers,  contractors,
homeowners,  and the general  public)  and Melad  & Associates,  Inc., and True North  Compliance  Services
will  help achieve  this City  Council  goal.

There  are several  large projects  in the planning  stages which  are pending  final  approval  and there is an
urgent  need to secure plan check  and inspection  services  providers.  Providing  a ready  list of additional
plan  check  firms  will  benefit  and expedite  service  to all developers,  designers,  contractors,  and the
general  public.

The cost for plan check  or inspection  services  is paid in advance  by the person,  company  or contractor
submitting  construction  requiring  the service.  Typically,  the breakdown  is a 35/65  split with  65% of the
collected  fee paid to the City  contracted  plan checker  for their  service.

  Plan Check Process

  Melad  & Associates  will provide  qualified  reviews  and plan check for completeness  and
  conformance  with  all City Ordinances,  State and Federal  Regulations,  and all adopted  Building,
  Electrical, Mechanical, Plumbing, Energy, Green Building, and Disabled Access/ADA codes. All
  reviews  will be performed  by our staff  of professionally  registered  engineers  and shall meet  all
  timetable  expectations.  At the City's  request  an in-house  plan checker  can be provided.

  The Melad  & Associates  Staff is qualified,  well versed,  and certified  to provide  the following
  types  of reviews.

  *  Structura

  A clear and concise  correction  list will be provided  with  all pertinent  building  information

  received  the plans or delivered  them  to the City.  It will set up a timeline  of the review  process
  in case there  are any questions,  and to help prevent  any possible  lag time.

  Digital  and Electronic  Plan Check Process

  Melad  & Associates  can send and receive  electronic  copies  of plans  using Dropbox  or other
  filing  sharing  services  of your  choice.  We can review  the plans,  calculations,  and other  related
  documents  using our Bluebeam  software  program.  We utilize  Microsoft  Word  to generate
  our corrections  lists that  can be sent back via email.  Each project  whether  submitted
  electronically  or paper  hardcopies  will have a unique  plan check  number  assigned  to the
  project.  This plan check  number  can be inputted  into our website  tracker  for the city or end
  users to get real time  updates  on each project.

  Melad  & Associates  can provide  accelerated  plan reviews,  meeting  timetable  expectations  put
  forth  in this proposal.  An applicant  may opt to submit  their  plans to Melad  & Associates  with
  the normal  turnaround  time  of ten to fifteen  working  days depending  on the size of the
  project  for the initial  review,  at the standard  rate put forth  by the City of South  Gate  Building
  Department  (65% of the plan check  fee).  The applicant  may also prefer  to reduce  the
  turnaround  time  of their  review  to 7 to 10  working  days for the initial  review,  at the standard
  rate put forth  by the City of South  Gate Building  Department  (65% of the plan check  fee),  plus

 GENERAL  INFORMATION

ABOUT  THE  CITY

The  City  of South  Gate  is located  in the southeastern  section  of Los Angeles  County  and
is approximately  seven  (7) square  miles  in  area.  The  City  shares  a common  boundary
with  the  cities  of  Downey,  Bell  Gardens,  Lynwood,  Cudahy,  Huntington  Park  and
Paramount.  South  Gate  is primarily  a residential  community  with  a current  population
of approximately  100,000.

The  City  was  incorporated  as  a general-law  city  in  1923  and  operates  under  the

Council/Manager  form of government.  The five (5) members of the City Council  are
elected  at large  by the residents  and serve  as the legislative  policy  making  body.  The  City
Council  has an appointed  five  (5) member  Planning  Commission.

The  City  is built  out  with  little  vacant  land  remaining.  However,  the age of the housing
stock  necessitates  ongoing  maintenance  and  additions.  Also,  the high  cost of housing  in
adjacent  cities  has  made  the  demolition  and  replacement  of  existing  homes  more
common.  With  respect  to commercial  activity,  the City's  ongoing  economic  development
efforts  and  private  development  continue  to create  infill  commercial  projects.  The  City
also has industrially  zoned  areas  where  infill  opportunities  exist.

City  Hall  hours  of operation  are 7:00 am  to 6:00 pm,  Monday  through  Thursday.  City
Hall  is closed  on Fridays.

BACKGROUND

The  City  of South  Gate  ("City")  is seeking  proposals  from  qualified  firms  for  plan  check
services  for  both  residential  and  non-residential  projects.  The  services  required  by  the
Building  and Safety  Division  will  include:  the review  of construction  drawings  to ensure
compliance  with  City  adopted  Building  Codes  and related  Municipal  Code  requirements;
providing  problem  solving  methods  for  unique  or  challenging  plan  check  or  code
interpretation  issues;  alternate  methods  of construction  and recommendations.

CURRENT  BUILDING  & SAFETY  SERVICES

The  Building  Division  is currently  staffed  with  following  positions:  one  (1) Building
Official;  one  (1) Senior  Building  Inspector,  two  (2) Building  Inspectors;  one  (1) Senior

 Counter  Technician;  one (1) Counter  Technician  III and two  (2) Counter  Technicians  II.
Plan check  services  are currently  provided  by contract  engineering  consultant,  Interwest
Consulting  Group.  Building  and  Safety  services  are  included  within  the  Building
Division  of  the  Community  Development  Department.  All  clerical  duties  (i.e.  fee
calculation,  permit  issuance  and  filing)  are conducted  by City  personnel.  The  selected
proposer  should  be able to provide  Plan Checking  services  to the City  as described  in this
RFP.

Currently,  the Building  Inspectors  work  Monday  through  Thursday,  which  is the City's
regular  work  week  - the  Community  Development  Department  operates  on  a 4/10
schedule.  The Building  Inspectors  are in the office  from  7:00 am to 9:00 am and in the
field  the remainder  of the day.  Each Building  Inspector  typically  conducts  inspections  at
10-20  sites per day.

The existing  contract  plan  checker  is available  over  the phone  and by appointment  to
South  Gate applicants  at the consultant's  office  Monday  through  Friday  from  8:00 am to
5:00 pm.  Additional  off-site  plan  checking  services  are provided  for mechanical,  electrical
and plumbing  (MEP).  The City  has a separate  consultant  to handle  all NPDES  issues.

A clear and concise correction list will be provided with all pertinent building information
stated at the top of the list (i.e., type of construction, group occupancy, scope of work, plan
check engineer), along with the current codes in use for the review. Two hard copies of the
correction list will be provided, one for the applicant and one for the City. The correction list
may also be emailed or faxed to the applicant or City at their request.

Upon approval of plan, two sets of plans, structural calculations, Title 24/Energy calculations,
and any other pertinent documentation will be stamped and wet signed by the plan check
engineer who completed the review. The plans will be delivered to the City directly by our on-
staff courier, and a return slip transmittal will be provided so that City Staff can sign and date
for the receipt of the drawings. This information will always help us in tracking the plans
whereabouts, and shall be inputted in our database, just as it was inputted at every time, we
received the plans or delivered them to the City. It will set up a timeline of the review process
in case there are any questions, and to help prevent any possible lag time.

Digital and Electronic Plan Check Process

Melad & Associates can send and receive electronic copies of plans using Dropbox or other
filing sharing services of your choice. We can review the plans, calculations, and other related
documents using our Bluebeam software program. We utilize Microsoft Word to generate
our corrections lists that can be sent back via email. Each project whether submitted
electronically or paper hardcopies will have a unique plan check number assigned to the
project. This plan check number can be inputted into our website tracker for the city or end
users to get real time updates on each project.

BUILDING PLAN REVIEW SERVICES
4LEAF will provide Plan Review for any type of structure to ensure compliance with all adopted codes, local
ordinances (including Tier 1 of Cal Green, if required) and State and federal laws that pertain to Building and
Safety, and for compliance with the adopted International Code Council (ICC) Building, Plumbing, Electrical,
Mechanical, National Fire Protection codes and standards, and the Accessibility and Noise and Energy
Conservation requirements as mandated by the State of California Title 24, State of California Water Efficient
Landscape Ordinance, the State of California Certified Access Specialist (CASp) compliance, and all other
applicable ordinances. The types of projects we provide these services for include Single-Family Dwellings, large
Multi-Family Mixed-Use Dwelling Units, Commercial, and Industrial.

Approach
We understand that the specific building plan review responsibilities will include, but are not limited to:
  • Examining plans, drawings, specifications, computations documents, soils reports, and additional data;
  • Ascertaining whether projects are in accordance with applicable building and fire codes, and City
  ordinances, including but not limited to Title 24 and Title 25;
  • Performing such reviews as structural, MEP, green building, fire and life safety, grading and drainage;
  • Reviewing plans to ensure conformity to the required strengths, stresses, strains, loads, and stability as
  per the applicable laws;
  • Reviewing plans to ensure conformity with use and occupancy classification, general building heights
  and areas, types of construction, fire resistance construction and protection systems, means of egress,
  accessibility, structural design, soils and foundations; and masonry;
  • Providing additional plan review services as requested by the City;
  • Conducting all plan review at the City Department or at a site mutually agreed upon in writing and;
  • Supplying all plan review staff with all code books and other basic professional references.

On- and Off-Site Review
4LEAF can supply Registered Professional Engineers to the City to work on-site performing structural plan review
and non-structural reviews at the jurisdiction’s discretion. Our experience includes checking for compliance with
the structural, life-safety, accessibility, plumbing, mechanical, electrical, fire, and local codes/ordinances.

Process Mapping
4LEAF aims to bring departmental processes together by identifying and eliminating obstacles to streamline
processes. Our subject-matter experts visit each department within a jurisdiction to conduct an analysis of
existing processes, identify how best to streamline separate departmental processes to improve workflow, and
provide guidance and recommendations on an improved work plan.

4LEAF implementation staff work both on- and off-site during this process and offer extensive training to
existing municipal staff members on the use of a jurisdiction’s preferred permitting software. We have a robust
amount of experience with software that aids in the implementation of process mapping, such as File Maker
Pro, OpenGov, e-PlanSoft, TRAKiT, EnerGov, Accela, and iWorQ.

 Plan Review QA/AC Review Process
Task 1 – Project Tracking Set-up
The first step of our process will be to set up the project in our system to enable 4LEAF and the City of South
Gate each to track the progress of the review. Our plan tracking procedures are designed to track each submittal
throughout the review process and maintain accurate and comprehensive records for each submittal.

Task 2 - Complete Submittal Review
Upon receiving the plans from the City, 4LEAF will triage (preliminary plan review performed by 4LEAF plan
review project lead) the submittal to verify that the submittal received is complete (i.e., all pertinent plans,
calculations, reports, and other related documents) in order that we can begin our review. If the submitted
package is incomplete, we will communicate with the City to discuss the deficient documents needed to proceed
with our review.

Task 3 - Plan Review Assignment
After the triage process is performed and a complete package is verified, the project will be assigned to the most
qualified Plans Examiner and a turnaround time will be established. We will log each application into our
database the same day the plans are received to assure that they are routed in a timely manner and to allow for
daily project tracking.

Task 4 - Plan Review
4LEAF will provide the project contact (Developer, Contractor, Architect, or Engineer) desired by the City of
South Gate with a list of any items needing correction and clarification to comply with applicable building codes,
ordinances, and regulations. A correction list will be created based on the missing codes and ordinances.

Task 5 - Quality Control
Prior to submitting the plan review correction list to the City, the designated plan review project lead will review
the correction list for adherence to applicable codes and ordinances as well as for accuracy and completeness.
After completion of our quality control review a correction list will be e-mailed to a designated staff member at
the City of South Gate or as directed by the City. The correction list and a 4LEAF transmittal form will include the
following information: a description of the work, type of construction, occupancy group, square footage,
number of floors, and sprinkler requirements.

Task 6 - Plan Review Rechecks
Plans received for rechecks will be reviewed for conformance. Our goal is to actively work with the designers to
resolve all unresolved issues after our second review. If it appears that there are complicated issues that might
cause a project to go beyond our second review, we will communicate directly with the designer to resolve
these concerns.

Task 7 - Project Approval
Once the final plan reviews are completed and ready for approval, 4LEAF will organize the plans and supporting
documents per the City of South Gate processing requirements and return them to the City, along with our
letter of completion.

   PROJECT APPROACH

Scope of Services
Allerion will provide plan review services for all residential and non-residential
building permit applications made to the City’s Department of Community
Development for the duration of the contract period of three years. This will
include initial plan reviews and subsequent rechecks or plan review comment
responses. Plan review will be performed in accordance with applicable state,
federal, and municipal codes as adopted by the City. Plans will be stamped and
signed by Allerion to indicate approval of the construction documents in a
manner acceptable to the City. Correspondence between permit applicants and
the off-site plan reviewer will be made available by phone and email. Any
correspondence from Allerion during the performance of this contract will be
clearly distinguished as a consultant of the City.

Transition from City’s Current Consultant
After the execution of this contract, Allerion will provide services for up to one
week at no cost to the City to meet with the current plan review consultant. The
goal of these meetings will be to review the current consultant’s services and
understand the expectations that the public may have from the City’s plan review
consultant. Permit documents that were reviewed by the current consultant that
are subsequently reviewed by Allerion during the performance of this contract
will be reviewed to the scope of the previously issued plan review comment letter
only. This scope restriction will be indicated on final approval letters. Permit
submittal documents in the possession of the City’s current consultant will need
to be transmitted to the City before they will be received by Allerion.

Permit Submittal Document Transportation
Allerion will provide transportation once per week for physical building and
construction plans or drawings, accompanying calculations and packages, and
other documents provided in relation to building permit applications.

Transition to Subsequently Adopted Code Cycle
The proposed duration of plan review services is likely to encompass a transition
of the currently adopted 2019 Edition California Building Standards Code to the
next triennial code cycle. As the City’s consultant, understanding the adoption
and enforcement dates for a code cycle transition is crucial to performing plan
review in accordance with the City’s municipal code. This change also
necessitates an update to plan review processes and standardized checklists.

As part of the triennial code cycle change, Allerion’s plan reviewers will complete
8 hours of training focused on the newly adopted code edition for the disciplines
which they review. The City’s Building Official shall alert Allerion to any changes
to the City’s municipal code which have an impact on Allerion’s plan review
services, including the effective adoption date.

PROJECT UNDERSTANDING
BPR understands the City of South Gate is in the southeastern area of Los
Angeles County and is primarily a residential community with an
approximate population of 100,000. The City is mostly built out with little
vacant land remaining but continues to see ongoing maintenance and
additions as well as demolition replacement of existing homes.
The current Building Division is staffed with one Building Official, one
Senior Building Inspector, two Building Inspectors, one Senior Counter
Technician, one Counter Technician III and two Counter Technicians II. In
addition to City staff, an outside consulting firm is also used to provide
Plan Check Services.
To maintain customer service levels, ensure timeliness of reviews and to continue to support the needs of the
department, the City is looking to partner with a qualified firm who can provide both residential and non-
residential plan review services. BPR has a team of experienced and appropriately licensed professionals
available to support the City in the requested services. From the RFP, we understand the Scope of Work is as
follows:
California Code of Regulation:
We understand that the City has adopted the 2019 California Code of Regulations, Title 24 (Part 1-
Administrative Code; Part 2-Building Code, Volume 1 and 2; Part 2.5–Residential Code; Part 3-Electrical Code;
Part 4–Mechanical Code; Part 5–Plumbing Code; Part 6–Energy Code; Part 8–Historical Building Code; Part 10–
Existing Building Code; Part 11–Green Building Standards Code; Part 12–Referenced Standards Code), IAPMO

Project Understanding and Approach to Work  S E C T IO N  3

T R AN SI T I ON P L AN
CSG recognizes the development successes of the City of South Gate and commits to a smooth transition of
Plan Check Services to ensure as little interruption as possible. CSG brings a fresh look at the services
currently being provided and welcomes an opportunity to review and make recommendations for
improvements if warranted. CSG proposes:
Onboarding
We suggest the initial onboarding of CSG start with a meeting or meetings with key stakeholders who will be
responsible for the complete workflow. The meeting will include a discussion of service level expectations;
review of the City’s permitting system and digital plan processing, comment creation and distribution;
establishing primary points of contact with direct access including access to assigned plan review staff; and
means of follow up communication to review services on a regular basis. CSG prides itself on the ability to
“hit the ground” running, but the onboarding will include determining any system and process training needs
and setting up training sessions for plan review team members. We would also like to meet with other
departments and staff to introduce ourselves, get to know the key City stakeholders, and initiate open
dialogue with them. We further propose to shadow the existing Plan Check Services staff for up to 3 days to
better understand the current functions, policies and procedures, and workflow–at no charge to the City.
We will then develop an internal process to address the City’s requirements. All of our CSG operations are
also supported by our experienced IT team which actively collaborates with existing client agencies to
integrate their systems with our plan distribution system to ensure efficient processing of review documents
within Bluebeam Studio.
Project Management Oversight
CSG’s project management philosophy is built upon the anticipation of, and preparation for, all issues that
may arise throughout a project and/or contract. Our project manager is seasoned and has years of
experience managing plan review contracts, transitioning between consultants/city staff, and ensuring
expected levels of service are achieved.
Communication Plan
CSG understands that clear communication with the City is vital to delivering the reviews successfully and
getting projects approved. This also allows us to gauge any potential issues and resolve them appropriately.
Internally, CSG conducts regular staff meetings where review progress and issues can be discussed to
determine ways to enhance review quality and, for example, eliminate duplication and conflicting comments
for the reviews that involve multiple disciplines. We also recognize that each jurisdiction is different and
during onboarding meetings we will work with the City to establish an efficient, straightforward
“Communication Protocol” which addresses the City’s needs.

P R OF E SSI O NAL C A P AC I T Y T O C OM P L ET E T A SK S
CSG has been performing plan review and inspection services for over 30 years and has honed its ability to
allocate and commit personnel to meet variable demand. As a result, with our large team of licensed and
certified plan review personnel, CSG successfully completes tens of thousands of plan reviews per year while
responding to variations and seasonality in clients’ plan check volumes and has achieved these results for
more than ten years while consistently maintaining accuracy, thoroughness and timeliness of reviews.
In addition, CSG has an exceptionally stable workforce and low staff turnover rate –with approximately 300
employees serving public agency customers throughout California and Nevada. This stability and strong
employee retention greatly contribute to our ability to ensure adequate resources are available to serve our
clients’ needs.

  All residential and non-residential plan checks will be performed by the selected firm. The selected firm will
  be required to review all building, plumbing, electrical, mechanical and related plans submitted to the City
  by private developers or other applicable government agencies for construction and reconstruction projects.
  Plans must be checked according to all applicable codes and statutes. All plans must be stamped and
  signed off if they meet all such requirements, and all changes/corrections must be identified and addressed
  prior to approval.

  appropriate “turnaround” times, are all key to the selection of a service provider. The proposal must include

Plan Review Process

Please note that our plan review process will be tailored to meet the City’s specific needs. The following process represents an
example plan review workflow which may be applied if desired by the City.

Step 1 - Preliminary Discussions:
  Prior to beginning our initial plan review project, our Project Manager proposes to conduct a meeting or conference
  call with the City to discuss local code policies, documentation procedures, plan processing protocols, plan review
  checklist items, and scheduling.
Step 2 – Initial Review:
  Once we receive a complete set of plan documents, we will perform our plan review in the agreed-upon timeframe,
  checking for compliance to all applicable code standards. To confirm, plan review turnaround timeframes will align with
  standard City-established timeframes. In general, project reviews are completed in 10 working days or less for initial
  reviews, and 5 working days or less for subsequent review cycles.
  All corrections are identified based on compliance with specified codes and regulations and worded so the designer will
  know what needs attention and how to respond to the issue stated. Generally, corrections are identified in two ways:
  •  Notes can be made on plans as appropriate and authorized to assist in locating the issue on the plans;
  •  A correction sheet is generated detailing what items need to be addressed before plans can be approved.
  The client will receive a copy of each correction list, as well as a cover memo containing the following:
  •  The date plans were reviewed by TRB and Associates
  •  The date that the applicant/applicant’s designee was notified that the plan review was completed
Step 3 – Transmittal of Plans and Comment Lists for Plan Review:
  At the heart of our approach in delivering our services to you, is the recognition that there must be a coordinated effort
  to track and coordinate all submittals and requests received. To help assure that submittals are properly coordinated
  and tracked, TRB and Associates has established an internal plan review coordination process to ensure that each plan
  received for review is properly handled, processed and returned on time. Our plan tracking procedures are
  computerized to track each submittal through the review process and maintain accurate and comprehensive records
  for each submittal. Upon completion of our review, any comments generated are consolidated into a correction letter
  which would then be forwarded to the City for its reference.
Step 4 – Rechecks:
  Upon receipt of the resubmittal package from the applicant, we will notify the City (via email) that we have received the
  package. Once we have verified that the resubmittal package is complete, we perform a recheck in the agreed-upon
  timeframe. This process is repeated until the project plan documents are ready to be recommended for approval.
Step 5 – Plan Approval:
  When all review comments are satisfied, we will forward two sets (or electronic equivalent) of all relevant correspondence
  bearing our company’s “Reviewed for Code Compliance” stamp (including plans, calculations, and specifications), along
  with a transmittal letter indicating our recommendation for project approval, and the project file to the City for
  processing.

Shipping and Delivery of Plans

TRB provides pre-printed overnight shipping labels and/or pickup services to facilitate the transport of plan submittals to our
office. Please note that the pickup, shipment and delivery of plan documents and other relevant correspondence to the City are
provided at no additional cost.

  Scope of Work
  When it comes to serving the residents of the City of South Gate community, Willdan sees our role as
  that of facilitator and guide—helping the City’s customers in getting through the review, permitting, and
  inspection process—rather than leaving the applicant in a bind in obtaining or signing off permits, while
  ensuring development complies with building codes and City standards. We understand that the
  process of complying with the various codes, standards, regulations and laws can be a formidable and
  daunting undertaking—for even the most seasoned design or construction professional. Furthermore,
  an understanding of the complexity associated with processing private development applications and
  the sometimes-competing interests is essential to exceptional customer service. Competing interests
  include, but are not limited to, creating a sense of place, achieving economic development objectives,
  ease of maintenance, and assuring the City will be as satisfied with the infrastructure on day one as 20
  years from “day one.” Common sense decision making and technical analysis in interpreting the intent
  of regulatory guidelines are significant strengths Willdan staff brings to the City.
  Our proven approach is based on years of experience and incorporates features enhancing the efficiency
  and quality of the following services:

  TRANSITION TO NEW CONSULTANT
  Willdan is aware that the City is currently using another service provider to provide plan review services.
  We understand that the transition from one consultant to another can be a timely and comprehensive
  situation. We keep this in mind whenever we are in this position by putting our client first and making
  the transition as smooth as possible.
  Our first step in the transition process will be to determine the status of all active permit applications
  and plan checks. We assume that all work performed to date on ongoing projects/assignments was
  conducted in accordance with all City requirements and state and federal regulations. This would allow
  Willdan to pick up where the current consultant left off, rather than starting the process over and,
  thereby, avoid any unnecessary delays. However, should any shortcomings be identified, they would
  immediately be addressed in order to ensure the timely and accurate completion of projects.
  The existing consultant would furnish project files, process status, timelines, and a list of outstanding
  issues for all current projects. Following the review of this material, Willdan will prepare an Excel
  spreadsheet that can assist the City and Willdan to determine the status of all projects and determine
  proper action.

SUBJECT:  RF,JECTION  OF  ALL  BIDS  FOR  THE  SGPD  HVAC  INSTALLATION
PROJECT,  CITY  PROJECT  NO.  667-GEN

PURPOSE:  The City  issued  a Notice  Inviting  Bids  for the SGPD  HVAC  Installation  Project.
All  of the bids received  were over budget  and are recommended  to be rejected.  The South  Gate
Municipal  Code requires  that the bids be formally  rejected  by the City  Council.

RECOMMENDED  ACTION:  The City  Council  will  consider  rejecting  all bids received  and
opened  on April  12, 2022,  in the City  Clerk's  Office  for the SGPD  HVAC  Installation  Project,
City Project  No. 667-GEN.

FISCAL  IMPACT:  None.

ANALYSIS:  The SGPD  HVAC  Installation  (HVAC)  Project  is a part of the Capital  Improvement
Program  and is budgeted  in the amount  of $65,000.  The project  entails  replacing  the HVAC
System  over  the jail  area. The scope  of the project  was required  to be expanded  during  design
which  resulted  in an engineer's  estimate  of  $190,000 and budget requirement  of $299,000,  The
HVAC  Project  was advertised  for construction  in the local  press and trade publications.  On April
12, 2022,  the City  Clerk's  Office  received  three bids all of which  were higher  than the engineer's
estimate  and  well  over  the project  budget  (See  Attachment  A).  The  table  below  provides  a
summary  of the bids received.  Staff  is recommending  that all bids be rejected.  Under  the South
Gate  Municipal  Code  Section  l.54.475  (Rejection  of  Bids),  the  City  has the  right  to reject
construction  bids at its sole discretion  by City  Council  action.  This right  was further  stipulated  in
the Notice  of  Inviting  Bids  (See  Attachment  B)  which  was  a part  of  the  construction  bid
documents.

  Engineer's  Estimate  $190,000.00

 The budget requirement to proceed with the project based on the bids is $525,000, which is not
recommended. An assessment of the South Gate Police Station's HVAC system identified several
issues that warrant improvements systemwide, such as, upsizing  the air-cooled chiller, replacing
the boiler, providing chilled, hot water piping and air handlers. As such, the proposed FY 2022/23
Capital Improvement Program includes :tunding for the SGPD HVAC and Renovation Project to
upgrade the HVAC system as recommended in the study. Staff will incorporate the subject HVAC
Project in lieu of proceeding as a standalone project, to achieve an economies  of scale savings.

BACKGROUND:  The HVAC Project is a part of the Capital Improvement  Program. It
originally entailed replacing two AC units over the jail area, modifying existing HVAC services,
providing horizontal fan coils, cooling and heating, providing supply/return air mains, laterals and
installing programable microprocessor-based thermostat  controls.

An agreement for design services was administratively  awarded to EDA, Inc., in the amount of
$9,900. During design, the scope of the project was augmented to include the following:  (a) a
third AC unit to solely service the Radio/Computer  Server Room, (b) temporary relocation and
resetting the equipment of the Dispatch Room, and (c) asbestos abatement of the ceiling area. This
caused the engineer's estimate to increase to $190,000 and the total budget requirement to increase
to $299,000. Design and construction documents were completed as of February 2022.

On February 22, 2022, the Notice Inviting Bids for construction was advertised in various trade
publications, the City website and in the local press. On April 12, 2022, three bids were received
in the City Clerk's Office. Pacific West Industries, Inc., was the apparent low bidder, with a bid
of $325,900 (See Attachment C), which exceeds the engineer's estimate of $190,000.

The Municipal  Code has requirements for rejecting bids. One requirement is that the bids be
formally rejected by way of a City Council action. Another requirement is that the City furnish a
written notice to the apparent low bidder at least two days prior to City Council rejecting the bids.
The Engineering Division issued such notice on July 14, 2022, to Pacific West Industries, Inc.,
(See Attachment  D).

SUBJECT:  CITY  CLERK  COMPENSATION

PURPOSE:  To continue  discussion  of City  Clerk  compensation  from  the July 12, 2022,  City  Council
meeting.

RECOMMENDED  ACTIONS:  The City  Council  will  consider:
  a.  Directing  staff  to prepare  a Resolution  which  would  adjust  the  City  Clerk's  compensation
  based on salary  and/or  benefits  stated in a City  Council  motion  and placing  said Resolution  on
  the August  23, 2022, regular  City  Council  meeting  agenda for,consideration.;  or
  b.  Approving  the existing  salary  and benefits  for the next term of office  of the elected  City  Clerk
  and no further  actiori  is needed.

FISCAL  IMPACT:  Unknown  at this time.  The precise  amount  of the financial  impact  will  depend
upon the action  taken by the City  Council  vis-A-vis  the City  Clerk's  salary/benefits.

ANALYSIS:  Pursuant  to state  law,  the  City  Council  sets the  salary  of the  City  Clerk  by  either
resolution  or by ordinance.  While  the salary  of a City  Clerk  may  be increased  during  the term  of
office,  the salary  of a City  Clerk  may  not be adjusted  downward  during  the existing  term  of office.
The City  will  hold  a General  Municipal  Election  on November  8, 2022,  in which  the City's  registered
voters  will  select  a City  Clerk.  The next  term  of office  will  commence  sometime  in December  2022
after the County  of Los Angeles  Board  of Supervisors  certifies  the results  of the election.

At the July  12, 2022,  City  Council  meeting,  the Council  received  public  testimony  on the matter  as
well  as amongst  themselves.  Based  on that  discussion,  the City  Council  requested  that  additional
information  be brought  back  which  could  assist  them  in understanding  the pros  and  cons  of the
potential  actions  they might  consider.  The requested  information  included  how  are other cities  staffing
their  City  Clerk's  Office  based  on the elected  being  fiill-time  or part-time?  What  might  those  costs
generally  be?

It may  be helpful  to restated  what  are the responsibilities  of the City  Clerk's  Office  in California.
Attachment  A is from  the California  City  Clerks  Association  outlining  what  the responsibilities  are for
the office.  It should  be noted that depending  on the size of the organization,  some of the duties  may be
handled  in a shared responsibility  with  another  department  or even additional  responsibilities  are taken
on by  the  Office.  What  is important  to note  is the  South  Gate  City  Clerk  position  is generally

The Office  of City  Clerk,  as previously  outlined  in Attachment  A, has responsibilities  and duties  that
require  full-time  operations  to meet  the needs  of  other  departments,  the  public  and other  elected
officials  who  seek  information,  signatures  on  contracts/documents,  and  acceptance  of many  legal
filings  (i.e.,  all FPPC  required  filings  and AB1234  Ethics  Training  Certifications).  Thus,  those cities
where  the elected  position  is not expected  to be in the office  full-time,  they provide  a position  that acts

Attachments  B thru H are a few of the job  specifications  for those  cities  within  the second  table that
are the day-to-day  managers  of the City  Clerk  Of':fice when the elected  City  Clerks  are not present.  Of
the seven (7) job specifications,  it should  be noted  that five  (5) of the seven require  a formal  education
of an Associates  of Arts  or in most cases a bachelor's  degree.  In six (6) of the seven, they require  that
the individual  have at least a Certified  Municipal  Clerk  (CMC)  ceitificate  at the time  of hire.

In the South  Gate  City  Clerk's  Office,  there  is currently  three  support  positions,  all titled  Records
Coordinator.  Their  job  specification  is reflected  in Attachment  I.  We are providing  this  as merely  a
reference  to compare  against  those  in Attachments  B through  H and its differences  from  those  in
scope, duties,  and requirements  than those listed  as the key position  within  those operations  where  the
elected  official  is part-time.  The City  Council  is cautioned  that discussion  beyond  this  simple  point
should  be avoided  in respect  of the incumbents,  who have stellar  work  history  and body  of work  that is
well appreciated.  In addition,  state law has many  limitations  when  discussing  a public  employee's
performance  or actions in a public  meeting.

However,  if the City  Council  decides  to reduce  the compensation,  then  it would  be reasonable  to
expect  that  the  elected  official's  presence  would  be diminished  considerably  in  the  office,  thus
potentially  impacting  timely  flow  of work  and record  keeping  commonly  associated  with  overseeing
an operations  department.  Thus,  to ensure the operations  continue  as expected,  there would  likely  need
to be an additional  position  added  similar  to the  Chief  Deputy  or Assistant  City  Clerk  positions
identified  in the second table above.

In fairness  of presentation,  many  of the speakers  at the last City  Council  meeting  emphasized  that the
vote on June 7, 2022, represented  that the community  did not whish  to change  the elected  status of the
City  Clerk,  nor the compensation  tied  to the position.  Those  speakers  indicated  having  a full-time
elected  City  Clerk  best serves the needs of the organization  and community

There  were  speakers  that expressed  concern  that, while  the previous  elected  City  Clerk  was a highly
qualified  expeit  City  Clerk,  the next  elected  City  Clerk  may  not  be or would  be less inclined  to
approach  the office  with  a full-time  desire.  Additionally,  it was expressed  that the next  elected  City
Clerk  would  most  likely  not have the experience  or education  level  associated  with  overseeing  a key
departtnent.

Finally,  the City  Council  inquired  if the City  Council  could  adopt  an ordinance  or resolution  that
would  establish  more  accountability  from  the elected  City  Clerk.  While  the City  Council  could  adopt
what would  amount  to their  belief  of how an elected  City  Clerk  should  perform,  state law prohibits  the
City  Council  from  placing  restrictions  or requirements  on the elected  office  in tei'ms  of hours,  policy
making  and operational  control.

caused  by  the  requested  reimbursement  rates  between  the  two  proposers  and  staffing  capacity.
