Additionally,  Compatior  is a much  smaller  organization  with  significantly  fewer  staff members  than
AltaMed  as a whole  organization.  However,  it should  be noted  that AltaMed's  proposed  Behavioral
Team  specifically  assigned  to this Program  is comparable  in size with  Compatior's  staffing.

As reported  previously  to the City  Council,  Compatior  proposed  an adjusted  rate of $75 per hour.
Acceptance  of that alternative  rate is up to the Council,  and, as stated,  was received  after the  scoring

process  had been completed.

Taking  all of the above  into  consideration,  staff  concluded  that both  organizations  are technically,
financially,  historically,  and professionally  qualified  to provide  mental  health  and counseling  services
required  by the solicitation.  However,  there  are principal  differences  between  the two  organizations
that  led  staff  to recornrnend  Compatior  for  the  City  Council  to consider.  Compatior  is a local
organization  that  established  its roots  in the City  of South  Gate,  and it has continued  to focus  its
services  primarily  on local  residents.  Eighty  percent  of its staff members  were previous  patients  and
are now paying  it forward  to serve their  own community.  Local  residents  helping  one another  provides

  4

  899
 a unique  cornmonality  between  service  providers  and patients  that would  otherwise  be more difficult
to duplicate  in a much  larger  organization.

AltaMed  serves a much  larger  population  and region,  namely  Los Angeles  and Orange  County.  South
Gate is one of many  cities  AltaMed  serves.  Both  organizations  provide  quality  mental  health  and
counseling  services,  however,  Compatior  has  differentiated  itself  from  AltaMed  through  its
commitment  to serve and focus  its services  primarily  towards  South  Gate residents.  Although  it is a
small  organization,  it has proven  its resilience  and commitment  to serve the community  through  the
pandemic.

With  City  financial  assistance,  Compatior  has served nearly  170 South  Gate residents  over the last 3
years. They  reported  serving  more with  other funding  contracts  they receive  from  third  parties.  Given
both organizations  are well  qualified  to deliver  the  services,  staff believes  Compatior's  appeals  to a
portion  of our community  that seeks a smaller  entity  to access services  for a variety  of reasons  that
will  go unserved  through  another  provider.  That is not to imply  that a provider  such as AltaMed  is not
accepting  or attempting  to reach out to such individuals.  As a result  of the pandemic,  we recognize
that many  residents  across the spectrum  prefer  and feel more  at ease in seeking  this  critical  service
from  a smaller  sized and more  accommodating  structure.

 Compatior  has no known  service  complaints  by clients  under existing  agreements  with  the City.  Their
pricing  is within  the approved  Los Angeles  County  reimbursement  rates for counseling  and mental
health  services.  Finally,  they have delivered  acceptable  services  underprevious  and current  agreements
for similar  services  called  for under this proposal.

Summary
The City Council  has three viable  options  to consider:  1) Award  the contract  to Compatior  as originally
recommended  by staff;  2) Award  contracts  to both Compatior  and AltaMed,  and appropriate  sufficient
funds from ARPA  or 3) Reject  bothproposals  and conduct  solicitationfor  mental  health  services  again.

BACKGROUND:  On July 26, 2022, the City  Council  continued  this item to the August  9, 2022, City
Council  Meeting  and directed  staff to provide  AltaMed's  response  to the solicitation  for mental  health
services.  On September  28, 2021,  the South  Gate City  Council  authorized  the City  Manager  to utilize
ARPA  funding  from  the United  States Department  of Treasury  for the Revive  South  Gate Spending
Plan,  which  includes  five  spending  categories:  recovery  from  the  pandemic,  direct  assistance
programs,  public  health  and safety,  critical  infrastructure,  and city  fiscal  health.  To respond  to needs
locally,  the City of South Gate has authorized  the expenditure  of up to $175,000,  annually,  for a mental
health  program  using  ARPA  funding,  with  two  one-year  possible  extensions,  including  certified
counseling  and clinical  services.

  A.  The American  Rescue  Plan Act ("ARPA")  was signed  into law in March  2021.  ARPA
  provides  funding  for a number  of different  programs,  including  the Coronavirus  State
  and  Local  Fiscal  Recovery  Fund  ("SLFRF"),  to provide  monetary  support  to local
  governments  to respond  to, mitigate,  and recover  from the COVID-19  public  health
  emergency.

  B.  On October  26, 2021,  the South  Gate  City Council  authorized  the City Manager  to
  utilize ARPA  SLFRF  funding  from the United  States  Department  of Treasury  for the
  Revive  South  Gate  Spending  Plan,  which  includes  five  spending  categories:
  recovery  from  the pandemic,  direct  assistance  programs,  public  health  and safety,
  critical  infrastructure,  and city fiscal  health.

The City of South Gate ("City"),  Department  of Community  Development  is pleased  to issue this
Request  for Proposals  (RFP) to solicit proposals  from qualified  Bidders  to provide  certified  mental
health counseling/clinical  services  in the City of South Gate. This RFP is being issued in response
to the needs  of the local community  and with American  Rescue  Plan Act (ARPA)  funds provided
for COVID-19  pandemic  relief. The City of South Gate is seeking  proposals  from qualified  Bidders
to provide  targeted  and timely  implementation  of mental  health services  identified  below to serve
the South Gate community  and its residents.

Proposals  are due by Thursday,  June  23, 2022,  by 4:00 PM. Proposals  may  be mailed  or
dropped  off.

 Overview
The  American  Rescue  Plan  Act of 2021  (ARPA)  was  established  to help  states  and
localities  address  the economic  and health  consequences  of the COVID-19  public  health
emergency  and its economic  impacts.  Since the start or the COVID-19  pandemic,  mental
health  symptoms  and substance  use have  increased.  This funding  opportunity  provides
support  to community  organizations  that are responding  to these  public  health emergency
impacts.  The awarded  applicant  will enter  into an agreement  with the City of South  Gate
to deliver  mental  health  services  to City residents.  Eligible  services  include  but are not
limited  to resource  navigation  support,  counselling,  and other  applicable  public  health
responses.  Awarded  contract  will be for up to $175,000  per year beginning  July 12, 2022,
with the possibility  of two, one-year  extensions.

Eligible  costs  are any  costs  associated  with  the planning,  coordination,  delivery,  and
administration  of the funded  programs.

Background
Globally  and nationally,  the COVID-19  pandemic  has negatively  affected  many  people's
mental  health and created  new challenges  for people  already  suffering  from mental  illness
and substance  use disorders.  As a result of these  pandemic  related  issues,  on March 11,
2021 President Biden signed the American Rescue Plan Act of 2021 (H.R. 1319) into
law. The ARPA  provides  $1.9 trillion  in additional  relief to respond  to the novel coronavirus
(COVID-19).  According  to the  u.s. Department  of the Treasury,  the Coronavirus  State
and Local  Fiscal  Recovery  Funds  (SLFRF)  provide  a substantial  infusion  of resources  to
help turn the tide on the COVID-19  pandemic,  address  its fallout,  and lays the foundation
for a strong  and equitable  recovery.

ARPA  includes  direct  assistance  to cities  to address  the  negative  public  health  and
economic  impacts  of the COVID-19  pandemic,  including  approximately  $34.5  million  to
the City of South  Gate ("ARPA  Funds").  The City of South  Gate coordinated  a process  of
community  engagement  which  included  listening  sessions,  meetings  with  community
partners  and  businesses,  an online  survey  tool,  and  City  Council  and  Commission
meetings  to hear what  South  Gate  residents  supported  as funding  priorities.  One of the
key themes  that arose  from this process  was a need for mental  health  services.

On September  28, 2021,  the South  Gate  City Council  authorized  the City Manager  to
utilize  ARPA  SLFRF  funding  from  the  United  States  Department  of Treasury  for the
Revive  South  Gate  Spending  Plan,  which  includes  five spending  categories:  recovery
from  the  pandemic,  direct  assistance  programs,  public  health  and  safety,  critical
infrastructure,  and city fiscal  health.  To respond  to needs  locally,  the City of South  Gate
has authorized  the expenditure  of up to $175,000  annually  for a mental health program
from ARPA  funding,  with two one-year  possible  extensions,  including  certified  counseling
and clinical  services.

Ideal  Proposals
This  program  will  contribute  to citywide  opportunities  for community  members,  which
contribute  to a continuum  of care  with  various  supports  being  available  to help  with
emotional  and mental  health  wellness,  and certified  clinical/counselling  services  paid on
a flat fee service.  Examples  include  therapy  groups,  skill building  or coping  skills groups,
activity  groups,  or faith-based  supports  which  aim to enhance  community  connections.
Services  and supports  must be easily  accessible  in a variety  of locations  throughout  the
City.  Counselling  and  clinical  services  and  support  must  be evidence-based  in their
practice  and must be available  in English  and Spanish.

Successful  bidders  will demonstrate  their  capacity  to evaluate  program  outcomes  and
collaborate  among  community  organizations  representing  different  sectors.  Approaches
should  include  equitable  and  inclusive  philosophies  with  target  populations  and
demonstrate  the potential  for proposed  sustainability  beyond  funding  provided.

Projects  should  address  the following:

  *  Screening,  Individual  Risk Assessment
  *  Counselling,  Individual  and Group  sessions
  *  Clinical  Services
  *  Mental  Health  Education  and Skill Development

Eligibility
Nonprofit,  tax-exempt  501 (c)(3),  u.s. organizations;  units of state or local government;  or
federally  recognized  tribal  communities  or tribes,  serving  the City of South  Gate,  may
apply.  This  can  include  neighborhood  organizations,  cultural  organizations,  places  of
worship/faith  organizations,  schools,  and  other  applicants.  Businesses  with  an active
registration  in good  standing  with  the  California  Secretary  of State  may  also  apply.
Funded  activities  must take  place  in the City of South  Gate  city limits  and serve  South
Gate residents.

The  bidder  must  identify  one  fully  burdened  hourly  rate  for  services  provided  in
association  with this RFP.  Rate of pay will be for staff time associated  with mental  health
screening,  individual  risk assessment,  counselling,  individual  and group sessions,  clinical
services,  and  mental  health  education  and  skill  development  for eligible  South  Gate
residents.  The  fully  burdened  rate  assumes  no  additional  reimbursement  will  be
processed  for  costs  associated  with  the  planning,  coordination,  delivery,  and
administration  of the proposed  program.  These  include  certain  training  costs,  community
engagement  and outreach,  site fees,  marketing  and outreach  materials,  administrative
expenses,  personal  protective  equipment  (PPE)  costs  associated  with program  delivery,
or other associated  costs with running  the proposed  project  or program.

identification  of a document  as "Confidential"  shall  not  be dispositive.  In making  a
determination  of whether  the information  is confidential,  the City uses the definition  of
trade secret  set forth in subdivision  (d) Section  3426.1  of the California  Civil Code,  which
states  "Trade  secret  means  information,  including  a formula,  pattern,  compilation,
program,  device,  method,  technique,  or process,  that: (1) Derives  independent  economic
value,  actual  or potential,  from not being generally  known  to the public or to other persons
who can obtain  economic  value from its disclosure  or use; and (2) Is the subject  of efforts
that  are  reasonable  under  the  circumstances  to maintain  its secrecy"  (Confidential
Information).  This  provision  does  not apply  to Confidential  Information  that is 1) in the
public  domain  through  no fault of the receiving  party, 2) was independently  developed  as
shown  by documentation,  3) is disclosed  to others  without  similar  restrictions,  4) was
already  known  by the receiving  party,  or 5) is subject  to disclosure  under  court  order  or
other  lawful process.

SUBJECT

Request approval to establish Fiscal Year 2020-21  Published Charges for the provision  of specialty
mental health services provided by the Department  of Mental Health's directly operated  clinics.

IT IS RECOMMENDED  THAT THE BOARD:

Approve  the Department  of Mental Health's  (DMH) proposed  FY 2020-21  Published  Charges,
effective  July 1, 2020.

PURPOSE/JUSTIFICATION  OF RECOMMENDED  ACTION

Approval of the recommended  action will allow DMH to make effective its proposed Published
Charges, reflected in Attachment 1, for use in billing the general public and third party payers for
specialty mental health services provided by DMH directly operated clinics, as permitted by law.

Implementation  of Strategic  Plan Goals
The recommended  action is consistent with the County's Strategic Plan Goal Ill, Realize Tomorrow's
Government Today, specifically Strategylll.3-  Pursue Operational Effectiveness,  Fiscal
Responsibility, and Accountability.

FISCAL  IMPACT/FINANCING

Approval of the requested  action will enable DMH to establish  a reasonable  approximation  of actual
costs for specialty mental  health services rendered.

There  is no net County  cost impact  associated  with the recommended  action.

FACTS  AND  PROVISIONS/LEGAL  REQUIREMENTS

The State Plan provides that Short-Doyle/Medi-Cal  (SD/MC) services are to be paid at the lower of
actual costs or customary  charges, which is consistent with federal Medicaid rules. The State has
implemented  such provision in the California Code of Regulations  Title 9 and in its cost reporting
instructions.  The term customary  charges is synonymous  with the term Published  Charges, which is
defined as the usual and customary  charges prevalent in the public mental health sector that are
used to bill the general public, insurers, and other non-Title XIX payers.

DMH contracts with the State Department  of Health Care Services (DHCS) as the local Mental
Health Plan (MHP) and provides specialty mental health services to Medi-Cal beneficiaries  under a
Section 191 5(b) waiver.  DHCS claims federal reimbursement  for Medi-Cal specialty mental health
services based on public expenditures  certified by the MHPs. When a MHP submits an interim claim
for reimbursement  it should either reflect the MHP's actual cost or a reasonable  approximation  of the
MHP's actual cost. When the claim for reimbursement  is for a specialty mental health service
rendered by a county owned and operated facility, the MHP is not expected to know its actual cost.
The MHP will not know its actual cost until the fiscal year is over and it has completed  its cost finding
and cost allocation  through the specialty mental health services cost report.  Consequently,  the
interim claim for reimbursement  of services rendered by county-owned  and operated providers will
be based upon a reasonable  approximation  of the MHP's actual cost, which are typically the lower of
1 ) Published  Charges or the 2) County Interim Rates, which are set by DHCS and based on the most
recent certified cost report submitted  by the MHP. DHCS will settle these interim payments  to actual
cost when the MHP files its certified cost report.

DMH's Published  Charges are determined  annually based on the most recent Annual  Cost Report,
projected cost increases, estimated  service delivery, and are adjusted by the Centers  For Medicare
and Medicaid Services Market Basket Index Levels.

In accordance  with Government  Code Section 66018, a public hearing will be held as required, prior
to the approval of a change to an existing fee. Special notice of that public hearing (Attachment  II),
in compliance  with Government  Code Section 6062a, has been published  by the Executive  Office.

IMPACT  ON CURRENT  SERVICES  (OR PROJECTS)

The recommended  FY 2020-21 Published  Charges will become effective on July 1, 2020. This
increase is not expected to negatively  impact mental health services to the public. With the
application  of the Uniform Method of Determining  Ability to Pay, as established  by State law, all
uninsured  DMH patients will most likely pay less than the Published  Charges.  Subsequently,  there  is
no anticipated  impact on current services.

CITY OF SOUTH GATE
  REGULAR CITY COUNCIL MEETING
  MINUTES
  TUESDAY, AUGUST 9, 2022
CALL TO ORDER  Al Rios, Mayor called a Regular City Council Meeting to order at 6:43 p.m.

INVOCATION  Steve Costley, Acting Director of Parks & Recreation
PLEDGE OF
ALLEGIANCE  Meredith Elguira, Director of Community Development

ROLL CALL  Yodit Glaze, City Clerk

PRESENT  Mayor Al Rios, Vice Mayor Maria del Pilar Avalos, Council Member Maria
  Davila, and Council Member Gil Hurtado; City Treasurer Greg Martinez,
  City Manager Chris Jeffers, City Attorney Counsel Raul F. Salinas

EXCUSED  Council Member Denise Diaz

COMMENTS FROM THE
AUDIENCE - NON-AGENDA
ITEMS  Jose Miranda explains last time he came, and the council decided to cut the
  time that the public could speak from five minutes to three minutes. He
  would like to know who had the idea to cut the time because last time they
  did not respond to his question. He expresses his discontent with this and
  says it is the United States it is not Venezuela, Russia, or North Korea.

  Henry Gonzalez says that April of last year he came to the Council meeting
  asking for help regarding a field or working with the school district to get a
  field for their games. Here he is a year later, and they have no home, and
  they reside in the equestrian area of South Gate Park. He explains that he
  has reached out several times and has not received a response. City
  Manager requested that he speak at Council meeting at four o'clock. He has
  invited the Council Members to the events and only Vice Mayor Avalos and
  Council Member Davila have shown up and it says a lot about them.

  Claudia Layton was here back in April to talk about the noise of the dairy
  company. Explains that nothing was ever done, and she spoke with one of
  the executives and they have stopped the noise at night for two weeks and
  then they continued. She called them again and it stopped, it has been four
  months of this. There was an accident in front of her window, says that that
  area has a lot of speeding problems. She would like help to get a stop or a
  slow sign on her street because there is no light or anything and they speed.
  Which makes her house shake and it happens day and night and is worse at
  night.
   REGULAR CITY COUNCIL MEETING MINUTES OF AUGUST 9, 2022

COMMENTS FROM THE
AUDIENCE - NON-AGENDA
ITEMS CONT'D  Carlos Amador says he spoke about his issues previously and would like to
  get them fix and he trust the Council will take care of his problems. Today
  he is here to talk about the inability to listen to the issues of residents,
  explains the trouble he had to go through to get his issues fixed. Now they
  have shortened the time for residents to speak, says the Council gets paid to
  be here.

  Robert Montalvo wants to echo a lot of the things that people have been
  saying regarding the reduction in time. Says Council doesn't respond to
  calls or emails which is why it is important for people to come to the
  Council meetings and speak. Also says that there is a 45 min cap which
  only allows fifteen people to speak and is wondering if they were aware of
  this. Another problem he finds is how they determine people to speak first if
  the in person or the zoom goes first. Thinks the Council should revisit the
  time of public speech.

  Liz Ruiz expresses her discontent with the new time limit, and she
  understands why they did it. She has a couple of things she wants to share,
  the first is the Air Quality Management District met last week and they are
  still working on the Community Commission Redevelopment Plan, there
  will be an annual report and it will be finalized soon and will provide
  council with updates. One thing that did come up is a presentation on a
  company in Vernon that sanitize a lot of medical equipment, and this
  company has been having big violation due to emissions from a chemical
  that increases a workers cancer risk. They are working on an agreement
  with the Air Quality District to fix a lot of those violations. She tried to
  speak on behalf of the community members who work at the factory and are
  being exposed to the hazardous conditions in addition to all the chemicals
  they are already exposed to in our community. The Environmental Safety
  Board will be having a meeting on the 25th of August in Sacramento, but
  they can log on online if they are interested. They will be discussing some
  of the changes that will be happening with the hazardous waste
  management plan, and they want to invite public.

  Irene Dates is here to talk about the way things are on California Street. For
  the past month the avenue has been taken over by racers and it is happening
  in front of the police department. Asks if they can have additional patrols in
  the area because it is making it difficult to sleep with all the noise.

  Thomas Buckley says campaign season is coming up and he hopes that they
  all remember their campaign promises and invitations to speak that were
  made to residents. Explains that many residents feel rushed to speak now
  because of the reduction in time to speak at Council meetings. He says this
  creates animosity between the residents and the Council because
  communication is key in any relationship. He hopes they can reconsider
  building and mending that relationship by inviting the residents to speak.

  Page 2 of 12
   REGULAR CITY COUNCIL MEETING MINUTES OF AUGUST 9, 2022

COMMENTS FROM THE
AUDIENCE - NON-AGENDA
ITEMS CONT'D  Mario Dominguez asked Chief Arakawa regarding the shooting in
  Monterrey Park. He says that he has never had any problems in Downey,
  but this is the second instance where he recalls another shooting involving
  an officer.

  Adolfo Varas currently serves as the Executive Director for Chamber of
  Commerce for Bell and he has an announcement. They have been working
  with the Senator Lena Gonzalez planning her first State of the 33rd District
  Address. It is scheduled for September 24th at 10am - 1 1 pm. He invited the
  Members of the City Council and the constituents that reside in the district
  to get to know her better and the things she has done for the community. He
  explains where everyone can go to RSVP for the event if they would like to
  attend it will be held at the Bell Community Center.

  Virginia Johnson thanked them for adjourning last Council it meant a lot to
  her. Also, thanked Liz Ruiz because she always has something pertinent to
  say to the community about events and meetings that concern everyone.

  Jose Gonzales is a resident of South Gate and would like to express his
  concern that he shares with some of the other residents. The first one
  regarding overgrown trees in the community. Trees that have not been cut,
  sidewalks that are cracked, and roots that are coming out of the sidewalk.
  Continues to talk about the city wasting money for measures and that the
  city should do their part to maintain the city and the residents will maintain
  their houses.

  Andrea Paulino doesn't understand people being offended by having a
  certain amount of time to speak. She proceeds to give advice on how to get
  through everything in the amount of time they are given.

  Ana, South Gate Chamber of Commerce thanked everyone for attending the
  grand opening of a Mexican restaurant right off Independence and Long
  Beach. She would like to extend an invitation for the grand opening
  tomorrow of Nova Storage, the ceremony will be held between 11 am —
  12pm.

  Yodit Glaze, City Clerk read an email from a resident who requested to
  remain anonymous. Resident is complaining about cars parking on Otis,
  they have flat tires and have been there for years. The resident has reached
  out to code enforcement, but nothing has been done and would like to know
  when the PD and code enforcement is going to enforce parking on unpaved
  surfaces.

  Page 3 of 12
   REGULAR CITY COUNCIL MEETING MINUTES OF AUGUST 9, 2022

REPORTS AND COMMENTS
FROM CITY OFFICIALS  Chris Jeffers, City Manager apologized to Mr. Gonzalez if he reached out
  regarding the football. Mr. Jeffers stated the mayor reached out to an
  LAUSD representative regarding an agreement with South Gate High
  School, and they are waiting for a response. Mr. Jeffers responded to the
  resident who spoke about the noise on the street, says he is unaware of the
  posted speed limit but that they do have a four-lane street and a lot of truck
  traffic goes through there and they could look at some speed enforcement.
  The city received a request to put up signs. Mr. Jeffers explained that the
  city cannot just put-up signs anywhere because they must follow state
  regulations. For the resident on Park Avenue, he had a conversation with
  the Public Works Director and is doing a follow-up tomorrow. The street
  sweeper is a more complex issue, but he will follow up with the Public
  Works Director. Mr. Jeffers will ask the Chief to look into the speeding on
  California. Mr. Jeffers took this moment to talk about what occurred at
  Monterrey Park and he expresses his condolences and willingness to help in
  any way they can. He refers to the resident who is concerned about the
  trees, he explains they are in the middle of a BID fund with the street tree.
  When the process is back maybe they can bring that process back by the
  23rd or the Pt. Tells the Council that the price of street cleaning is going up
  and that is something that should be asking for substantial funds to make
  that possible. Says if there are any trees or sidewalks, he encourages them to
  email him. Mr. Jeffers is going to have engineering look at any engineering
  issue on Southern Avenue and PD to look at parking violations.

  Mayor Rios says that the reduction in speaking time has been discussed a
  lot in the public comments. He explains that the Council has been looking
  for ways to reduce the time the meetings and they still have a chance to talk
  at the end of the meeting. Explains that neighboring cities have an overall
  three minutes and are not allowed to talk at the end of the meeting.

  Meredith Elguira, Director of Community Development announced that
  they accept credit card now as a form of payment at the Community
  Development counter.

  Arturo Cervantes, Director of Public Works nothing to report.

  Darren Arakawa, Chief of Police nothing to report.

  Chris Jeffers, City Manager explained that the Chair does have the ability to
  extent the time to speak depending on the need or the topic. He would like
  to note for the record that it was only 28 minutes for the oral
  communication that occurred today. Explains that if this is a problem the
  Council does have the ability to change the procedures and rules moving
  forward from that standpoint.

  Page 4 of 12
   REGULAR CITY COUNCIL MEETING MINUTES OF AUGUST 9, 2022

REPORTS AND COMMENTS
FROM CITY OFFICIALS
CONT'D  Raul F. Salinas, City Attorney spoke on the timing issue says he
  understands the Council took that issue to heart. Says this subjecting is
  going to be constantly monitored by the City Council. Explains all the time
  that people are allowed to speak aside from the public comments and
  compares to other cities that limit the public speaking and explains it is
  balancing act and they will continue to monitor it to see how everything
  works out.

  Chris Jeffers, City Manager would like to add that he and the City Attorney
  will be hosting a meeting on the Brown Act on August 25th at 6:30 and it
  will be held in person and zoom. The intent is to educate the public about
  the Brown Act.

  Yodit Glaze, City Clerk explained that if they are unable to attend the
  meetings in person or through zoom, they can email the city clerk and she
  can read the comments.

  Greg Martinez, City Treasurer spoke regarding the limitation on the time of
  speaking. Explains that if an outside person came to speak like the State
  Assembly Member, then they would take up the time of the residents
  because of the 45-minute time block. Says that some residents get frustrated
  and sometimes they feel they are not being heard and might walk out.

  Council Member Davila recalls that for the past two years some of the
  comments have not been related to city business and sometimes they got out
  at one or twelve thirty. The reason they are trying this is to allow the
  residents to have a voice because sometimes they have twenty speakers and
  five minutes. Some of the speakers that speak have nothing to do with city
  business, explains that they are here to listen to the concerns of the residents
  regarding streets, sidewalks, or other city issues. Says if this something very
  important like the accident example provided by the City Treasurer, they
  will of course listen because it is a priority. Explains that they will not stop
  them from speaking and hopes that they understand they are trying this out.
  Council Member Davila stated that City Manager receives many calls, but
  she has not received any calls about the reduction in time.

  Arturo Cervantes, Director of Public Works explained that there are two
  types of contracts the one they used to do the long term one and the as
  needed services. When they don't have the first contract, they use the as
  needed service contract. They are currently going through the RFP process
  to get a longer contract; they currently have a contract in place for as needed
  services when emergencies arise.

  Page 5 of 12
   REGULAR CITY COUNCIL MEETING MINUTES OF AUGUST 9, 2022

REPORTS AND COMMENTS
FROM CITY OFFICIALS
CONT'D  Council Member Davila explained that those are some of the issues that
  they need to take care of, and she wants to hear from the residents. To
  follow up on her reports, she mentioned that the Executive Director for Eco-
  Rapid Transport is leaving, and they are still in the process of filling the
  position. They do hope that by next month they have someone to fill that
  position.

  Council Member Hurtado stated on Saturday, August 18th will be a
  backpack give away at the ELAC campus. Hopes everyone is save with the
  school year coming up and covid. Says the golf course is a great place to
  make it a football field because they are not getting many visitors.
  Expresses that he did not agree with the reduction in time for public
  comments and explains some of the reasons why. Council Member Hurtado
  says that when people come in and talk about the street cleaning or other
  things that need to be fixed and we say we are going to fix it, but we do not
  that should not be happening.

  Vice Mayor Avalos agree with Council Member Davila. She explains she
  listens to every constituent when they email her or call her and tries to help
  when she can. She says it would be nice if things could be handled in a
  timely matter and the fact that it is not is disappointing and does not sit well
  with her. Another thing that does not sit well with her is when people say
  there is corruption and explains that they can call their local officials to get
  to the bottom of things. Explains that they are doing the peoples work and
  the reduction in time is to see if it will work, it can be changed but they are
  trying to serve the people of South Gate as best as possible. Says it is sad
  that there is a lot of misinformation especially because elections are here
  and would like to clear up one thing and put it on the record. She speaks
  regarding the matter of a candidate running for office, her name is Crystal
  Tapia, and she works at the same school district as Vice Mayor Avalos.
  Vice Mayor states she does not know Ms. Tapia and did not tell her to run.
  She attended a water board meeting last Thursday with the Southeast Water
  Coalition, and two issues came up, she will be directing the issue to the
  Director of Public Works. The first issue is regarding the possibility of
  joining a lawsuit against 3M and other manufacturers that have contributed
  to the toxic contamination with Downey and Pico Rivera. The other issue is
  about the possibility of securing a grant to address the payoffs the timeline
  for the grant is August 15th, 2022.

  Arturo Cervantes, Director of Public Works explained that he did receive
  the email but did not get the opportunity to review it, but he will provide
  Vice Mayor Avalos information. Regarding funding for remediation, the
  city took initiative about a year or year and a half ago and they have already
  obtained between 2 -3 million dollars. If she is referring to the 1 billion
  dollars funding that is available, it is available for the state funding the city

  Page 6 of 12
   REGULAR CITY COUNCIL MEETING MINUTES OF AUGUST 9, 2022

REPORTS AND COMMENTS
FROM CITY OFFICIALS
CONT'D  will not be applying for that grant, but he can give her more information as
  to why.

  Vice Mayor Avalos thanked Mr. Cervantes for that information. She
  explains that at her school district they have something called professional
  development and she attended it today. It has to do with emotions of the
  students and teachers and how those emotions are transmitted. The issue of
  respect was brought up and she read something on the meaning of respect.
  Vice Mayor has respect for her community and will always respect her
  community.

  Mayor Rios says communication in terms of the new reduction in time, he
  would like people to know that they can call, email, contact the city clerk or
  other staff members and make appointments to meet with council. Explains
  that there are other ways of getting into contact with the city staff or council
  and that coming to council meetings to speak should be a last resort. Part of
  the reason they changed the time is because they have businesspeople here
  waiting, contracts to sign, and they were getting to them late. Council
  Member Hurtado mentioned the event at the ELAC campus, and he stated it
  is a drive thru event. They will start lining up at 8 and beginning giving out
  backpacks at nine until the supplies runs out. Mentions that school will be
  starting on the 15th and that ELAC starts the 29th they will be having an
  enrollment day on August 20th. Also reminding people of the new water
  regulations and they have a meeting schedule with Jackie Goldberg
  regarding school safety with school officers getting cut. Wants to highlight
  one thing that they did, the council funded a tutorial for the kids that have
  fallen behind and the Vice Mayor was also in attendance. Describes that he
  is proud of the council for all their hard work and, they plan to do it again in
  the fall.

  Council Member Davila asked if she could attend the meeting with Jackie
  Goldberg. She also asked if crossing guards can be placed on Willow Place
  and Santa Fe Avenue.

  Darren Arakawa, Chief of Police explained they did investigate getting a
  crossing guard increase to have those two intersections covered. There is a
  cost for that.

  Chris Jeffers, City Manager explained that they were going to bring it up
  during the budget meeting to discuss this.

  Council Member Davila says this is worth it because the children need to be
  kept safe.

  Mayor Rios says it is also important to have the conversation regarding
  crime and homelessness in the community and along the river.

  Page 7 of 12
   REGULAR CITY COUNCIL MEETING MINUTES OF AUGUST 9, 2022
REPORTS AND COMMENTS
FROM CITY OFFICIALS
CONT'D  Council Member Davila would like to be included in that meeting and asks
  if they can enlighten them regarding the collaborative.

  Chris Jeffers, City Manager informed the public that Council Member
  Diaz's father had a heart attack and that is the reason she is unable to attend.
  He asks that they keep her family in their thoughts and prayers.

CONSENT CALENDAR  Agenda Items 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 7 and 8 were approved by motion of Council
  Member Davila and seconded by Vice Mayor Avalos. Item 5 was pulled
  for separate discussion.

  ROLL CALL: Council Member Davila, yes; Council Member Diaz,
  absent; Council Member Hurtado, yes; Vice Mayor Avalos, yes; Mayor
  Rios, yes
1
MUNICIPAL CODE
ADMIN  The City Council waived the reading in full and adopted Ordinance No.
  2022-07-CC entitled Ordinance of the City Council of the City of South
  Gate, California, amending Chapter 11.33 (Parking Standards), of Title 11
  (Zoning), of the SGMC to include parking requirements and standards for
  land uses serving children, older adults, community assembly or people
  with disabilities, during the Consent Calendar.
2
CITY MEMBERSHIPS  The City Council adopted Resolution No. 2022-46-CC entitled Resolution
  of the City Council of the City of South Gate, California designating a
  member of the City Council as the voting delegate for the Annual Business
  Meeting/General Assembly during the 2022 League of California Cities
  Annual Conference and Expo and up to two (2) alternate voting delegates
  should the primary designee be unable to represent the City, approved
  during the Consent Calendar.
3
PERSONNEL RECRUITMENT
& SELECTION  The City Council adopted Resolution No. 2022-47-CC entitled Resolution
  of the City Council of the City of South Gate, California amending
  Resolution No. 6454 (Salary Resolution and Position Classification Plan) to
  update the job specifications and salary range for the position of Housing
  Administrator to Housing Manager in the Community Development
  Department and reassigning the Housing Manager position as an Executive
  Management Contract Employee, update the job specifications and salary
  range for the Deputy Director of Parks & Recreation and Parks
  Superintendent in the Parks & Recreation Department and to update the
  salary range for the position of Deputy City Engineer in the Public Works
  Department, during the Consent Calendar.

  Page 8 of 12
   REGULAR CITY COUNCIL MEETING MINUTES OF AUGUST 9, 2022

4
WATER ISSUES/SYSTEM
ADMIN  The City Council approved items A & B during the Consent Calendar:

  a. Agreement (Contract No. 2022-63-CC) with John L. Hunter and
  Associates, Inc. ("Agreement"), for storm water management services
  required by the National Pollution Discharge Elimination System
  (NPDES) Permit, for a three-year term, in an amount not-to-exceed
  $334,155, or $111,385 annually; and

  b. Authorized the Mayor to execute the Agreement in a form acceptable to
  the City Attorney.

5
PUBLIC ASSISTANCE  The City Council approved items A, B, C, D & E by motion of Council
  Member Davila and seconded by Council Member Hurtado:

  ROLL CALL: Council Member Davila, yes; Council Member Diaz,
  absent; Council Member Hurtado, yes; Vice Mayor Avalos, no; Mayor
  Rios, recused

  a. Agreement (Contract No. 2022-64-CC) with Hub Cities Career Center
  ("Agreement") to perform an inventory of newsracks and pay phones in
  the public right-of-way for a not-to-exceed amount of $34,500;

  b. Authorized the City Manager to execute the Agreement in a form
  acceptable to the City Attorney;

  c. Approved appropriation of $45,000 from the Refuse Collection Fund to
  fund the Agreement and all anticipated staff costs with implementation
  of the described program;

  d. Directed staff to begin notification to permittees of abandoned,
